 Choose the Right Synonym for _open_

[frank](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/frank), [candid](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/candid), [open](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/open), [plain](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/plain) mean showing willingness to tell what one feels or thinks.

[frank](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/frank) stresses lack of shyness or secretiveness or of evasiveness from considerations of tact or expedience.

_frank_ discussions

[candid](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/candid) suggests expression marked by sincerity and honesty especially in offering unwelcome criticism or opinion.

 a _candid_ appraisal 

[open](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/open) implies frankness but suggests more indiscretion than [frank](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/frank) and less earnestness than [candid](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/candid).

_open_ in saying what they think

[plain](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/plain) suggests outspokenness and freedom from affectation or subtlety in expression.

_plain_ talk

[liable](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/liable), [open](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/open), [exposed](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/exposed), [subject](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/subject), [prone](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/prone), [susceptible](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/susceptible), [sensitive](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/sensitive) mean being by nature or through circumstances likely to experience something adverse.

[liable](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/liable) implies a possibility or probability of incurring something because of position, nature, or particular situation.

_liable_ to get lost

[open](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/open) stresses a lack of barriers preventing incurrence.

 a claim _open_ to question 

[exposed](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/exposed) suggests lack of protection or powers of resistance against something actually present or threatening.

_exposed_ to infection

[subject](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/subject) implies an openness for any reason to something that must be suffered or undergone.

 all reports are _subject_ to review 

[prone](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/prone) stresses natural tendency or propensity to incur something.

_prone_ to delay

[susceptible](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/susceptible) implies conditions existing in one's nature or individual constitution that make incurrence probable.

 very _susceptible_ to flattery 

[sensitive](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/sensitive) implies a readiness to respond to or be influenced by forces or stimuli.

 unduly _sensitive_ to criticism 

## Examples of _open_ in a Sentence

Adjective The door suddenly swung _open_.  You left the blinds _wide open_.  The meat was roasted over an _open_ fire. 

 I was so tired that I couldn't keep my eyes _open_.  Don't chew with your mouth _open_.  staring with her eyes _wide open_ There's already an _open_ jar of pickles in the refrigerator.  They kept the road _open_ throughout the winter. Verb This door is hard to _open_.  “_Open_ the door!” shouted the police officer.  Would you mind if I _opened_ a window?  The car door _opened_ and a beautiful woman stepped out.  The door _opened_ and closed so quietly that I didn't notice he had come in the room.  This drawer is stuck. It just won't _open_!  She comes home, turns on the TV, and starts _opening_ her mail.  She _opened_ her eyes and smiled at me.  I _opened_ my umbrella and stepped out into the rain.  “_Open_ your mouth wide for me,” said the dentist. Noun a daguerreotype of a cowboy whose face is roughened from a hard life in the _open_

a
